key_headlines.title: Won Weakens to Lowest Level Since 2009 Financial Crisis Despite Trade Surplus
key_headlines.summary: Despite 36 consecutive months of current account surplus exceeding 43 trillion won, the Korean won plummeted to 1,539 won per dollar due to foreign investor stock market exodus and structural factors, marking the weakest level since the 2009 global financial crisis.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Plunges 5.5% on Broadcom Shock and Foreign Investor Selloff
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI index fell 478.82 points (5.54%) to 8,160.59 following disappointing guidance from U.S. semiconductor firm Broadcom, triggering a massive foreign investor sell-off and pushing the won-dollar exchange rate to historic weakness of 1,549 won.

key_headlines.title: Labor Minister Emphasizes AI Profit Sharing as Reinvestment, Not Communism
key_headlines.summary: Labor Minister Kim Young-hoon stated that distributing semiconductor companies' excess AI profits represents legitimate reinvestment through social dialogue, proposing contract price adjustments with suppliers as a cooperation measure.

sections.Hot Economy News: Korea's economy demonstrated exceptional strength with Q1 GDP growth of 1.7% quarter-over-quarter, the highest among OECD nations, driven by semiconductor export surge exceeding 390 billion dollars in January-May (40% increase year-over-year) and sustained current account surpluses. Vice Minister Huh Jang promoted Korea's economic achievements at investor briefings in Paris, emphasizing capital market reforms and recent World Government Bond Index inclusion attracting 18.7 billion dollars in foreign bond inflows. However, despite strong economic fundamentals, the Korean won weakened significantly to 1,539 won per dollar, marking the weakest level since the 2009 financial crisis, reflecting foreign investor portfolio rebalancing despite positive domestic indicators.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Korea's macroeconomic performance remains robust with Q1 GDP growth of 1.7% quarter-over-quarter and a consecutive 36-month current account surplus exceeding 43 trillion won, positioning the country among the strongest performers in the OECD. The government is pursuing expansionary fiscal policy initiatives including fast-track approval for the 400 billion won Jangseong data center project and plans to accelerate private sector redevelopment and reconstruction projects in Seoul targeting 310,000 housing units by 2031. The Bank of Korea appointed new deputy governors for research and statistics (Lee Ji-ho) and management (Kim Je-hyun), signaling continuity in monetary policy while facing inflation pressures from oil price increases, with market expectations of potential rate hikes in July.
sections.Financial Markets: Korean financial markets experienced significant volatility and weakness, with KOSPI plunging 5.54% to 8,160.59 points triggered by disappointing guidance from U.S. semiconductor firm Broadcom regarding AI chip demand and subsequent foreign investor selloff. The won-dollar exchange rate surged to 1,539 won per dollar, reaching levels not seen since the 2009 global financial crisis, while 10-year government bond yields rose 2.5 basis points to 4.254% annually. Foreign investors triggered the sell-side circuit breaker (program trading halt) for the tenth time this year, reflecting deteriorating sentiment, and the market faces ongoing pressure from SpaceX's IPO scheduled for June 12 expected to trigger liquidity outflows.
sections.Industry & Technology: Korean shipbuilders are accelerating development of eco-friendly vessels powered by small modular reactors (SMR) and biofuels to capitalize on strengthening global environmental regulations, with HD Hyundai Heavy Industries and HD Korea Shipbuilding receiving concept design approvals. Korea Zinc announced its large-scale Australian energy project with battery capacity equivalent to 26,000 Tesla Model Y electric vehicles, surpassing South Korea's largest ESS facility by sixfold. TSMC confirmed additional land acquisition near its Arizona Phoenix 21 fab to accommodate major customers' AI infrastructure demands, while CEO Jensen Huang's visit to Korea highlighted the nation's exceptional AI and robotics expertise alongside world-leading semiconductor, automotive, and battery manufacturing capabilities.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's real estate market faces critical challenges with soaring jeonse (long-term lease) deposits and plummeting supply, prompting newly elected Mayor Oh Se-hoon to identify housing as the top municipal priority and warn of potential real estate crisis without policy direction changes. Officetels gained popularity as a substitute for apartments, with Seoul jeontel (full lease/monthly rent) transactions increasing 9.1% year-over-year to 34,278 units in January-April, driven by apartment jeonse scarcity declining 28.7% year-over-year to 18,455 available units. Price-capped apartments under the Housing Cost Ceiling System showed competition rates 2.5 times higher than uncapped developments as consumers sought more affordable options, while Mayor Oh's re-election with strong support from southern districts like Gangnam suggests accelerated momentum for private reconstruction projects.
sections.International Economy: The U.S. Federal Reserve's Beige Book indicated expanding energy-driven inflation pressures and stalled employment, with markets expecting the FOMC to hold rates steady at its June 16-17 meeting while acknowledging renewed inflation risks from Middle East tensions and oil price increases. Financial markets have significantly shifted expectations on December rate hikes from 9.1% to 41.1% probability within a month, reflecting growing hawkish sentiment among Fed officials including Trump-aligned members. Investment research houses recommend a June allocation preference ranking of United States-Europe-Japan, with SpaceX IPO completion and FOMC resolution expected to reduce uncertainty and potentially support index gains, though medium-term uncertainties from China's transshipment prevention measures and forthcoming CPI data persist.
sections.AI & Economy: Labor Minister Kim Young-hoon characterized semiconductor companies' AI profit distribution as legitimate reinvestment rather than communist redistribution, proposing supplier contract price adjustments as a cooperation mechanism to share AI boom benefits across supply chains and society. Goldman Sachs projected SpaceX's AI business revenue growing approximately 100-fold by 2030 during its IPO roadshow, indicating AI operations must experience explosive growth for the 1.77 trillion dollar valuation to materialize. TSMC confirmed additional Arizona land acquisition to meet major customers' accelerating AI infrastructure investment demands, while regulatory concerns emerged regarding Chinese firms potentially acquiring latest Nvidia AI chips despite U.S. export controls with possible loopholes in restrictions implemented since 2023.
sections.Others: Korea's 2023 trade agreement baseline is expected to largely remain intact despite Trump administration application of Trade Act Section 301 tariffs, though pressure on preventing Chinese transshipment of products continues to mount. The Food and Drug Administration approved a new ultrasound surgical device for renal nerve ablation to treat resistant hypertension when lifestyle modifications and medications prove insufficient, expanding treatment options for hypertensive patients. KATIS secured a 5.81 billion won contract with Daelim for Gimpo data center security and IT infrastructure construction work representing 20.82% of recent revenues, reflecting continued strong demand for data center security infrastructure amid expanding AI investments.
